authority: LegalEase Mississippi Definitive Route Decisions (2026-08-24) and the Mississippi Override Register

routes.mechanism: DUI nonadjudication

timing.anchorText: no elapsed wait; admission occurs while the case is active, and the final order follows court-certified completion

requiredFacts: Is the case active or unadjudicated?
Which DUI subsection and court is the matter under?
Does the person hold a CDL or CLP?
Any prior DUI nonadjudication or expunction?
Have all court-ordered conditions been completed?
exclusions: No prior DUI nonadjudication or expunction
routes.notes: Never apply the five-year first-offense-DUI expungement rule to this route. Attorney-assisted motion/order only where supported.

routes.mechanism: Eligible felony conviction expungement
routes.statute: Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-71(2), as amended by 2026 Miss. H.B. 1546

timing.anchorText: three years after court-certified successful completion of all terms, with every fine and cost paid; where records conflict, use the later reliable completion or payment date

processingDeadlines.label: 10-day district attorney notice
processingDeadlines.note: a service step inside the petition, not a participant eligibility wait

requiredFacts: Do the counts arise from a common nucleus of operative facts?
Has the full sentence been completed?
Are all fines, costs and restitution paid?
Was the person a public official and was the offense connected to that office?
How will the district attorney be served?
routes.packetFamily: Petition for Expungement of an Eligible Felony Conviction under § 99-19-71(2)
packetComponents: Proof of sentence completion and zero balance

supersedes.note: the stale five-year rule that governed filings before 2026-07-01

routes.notes: Use three years, not the stale five-year rule, for current filings on or after 2026-07-01.

routes.mechanism: First-offender nontraffic misdemeanor expungement

timing.anchorText: no numeric waiting period; relief unlocks on the final qualifying first-offender nontraffic misdemeanor conviction

requiredFacts: Is the offense a traffic violation or otherwise under Title 63?
What is the complete conviction history?
routes.notes: Do not use § 99-19-72 as eligibility authority.

routes.mechanism: Controlled-substance conditional discharge — admission to deferred adjudication

timing.anchorText: admission is active-case relief sought while the prosecution is live; no elapsed wait applies

requiredFacts: Any prior use of conditional discharge?
routes.notes: Split from the post-completion packet stage. No generic wait, and no consumer checkout while the case is active.

routes.mechanism: Controlled-substance conditional discharge — expungement after discharge and dismissal

timing.anchorText: expungement opens on the discharge-and-dismissal order date, after successful probation

requiredFacts: Any prior use of conditional discharge?
What are the probation dates and was compliance complete?
routes.notes: Checkout opens only after discharge and dismissal.

routes.mechanism: Human-trafficking survivor relief — remedy selection between vacatur and expungement
routes.statute: Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6(5)-(6), as amended by 2026 Miss. H.B. 1546

timing.anchorText: available at any time once the covered offense and the trafficking nexus are established; no elapsed clock

requiredFacts: Is the offense a violent offense?
Is the person seeking vacatur, expungement, or both?
What are the trafficking dates, nexus and evidence?
routes.notes: Retained as the selection route only. The two statutory remedies are separate contracts and each requires attorney review; this route never sells a packet on its own.

routes.mechanism: Human-trafficking survivor vacatur
routes.statute: Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6(5), as amended by 2026 Miss. H.B. 1546

timing.anchorText: available at any time on the conviction or adjudication plus the trafficking nexus; no elapsed clock

requiredFacts: What are the trafficking dates, nexus and evidence?
Can the direct-result nexus be shown by a preponderance?
routes.notes: Mandatory attorney review before any packet is produced. Never import the ordinary felony wait.

routes.mechanism: Human-trafficking survivor expungement
routes.statute: Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6(6), as amended by 2026 Miss. H.B. 1546

timing.anchorText: available at any time on the covered offense plus the trafficking nexus; no elapsed clock

requiredFacts: Is the offense a violent offense?
What are the trafficking dates, nexus and evidence?
exclusions: Violent-offense exclusion applies to the expungement branch
routes.packetFamily: Petition or Motion to Expunge under § 97-3-54.6(6)
packetComponents: Petition or motion to expunge under § 97-3-54.6(6)
routes.notes: Mandatory attorney review before any packet is produced. The violent-offense exclusion applies here but not to vacatur.

routes.mechanism: Intervention-court completion — automatic statutory result for the sentenced-at-plea branch

timing.anchorText: the statutory result follows court-certified successful completion of every requirement, including nonwaived obligations

requiredFacts: Was a sentence imposed at the plea?
Has the docket already been expunged?
routes.notes: Checkout and packet credit stay closed on this branch: the statute clears the record, and the product verifies status and guides correction.

routes.mechanism: Intervention-court completion — dismissal-only branch where a record remains

timing.anchorText: relief opens on the dismissal following court-certified completion, where a record remains

requiredFacts: Was a sentence imposed at the plea?
Was the case dismissed rather than sentenced?
exclusions: Sentenced-at-plea matters belong on the automatic branch
routes.notes: The only intervention-court branch that may sell a packet.

routes.mechanism: Intervention-court completion — enforcement of the statutory result

timing.anchorText: used once completion is certified but the court or agency has not carried out the statutory result

requiredFacts: What does the docket currently show?
Has the docket already been expunged?
routes.notes: Enforcement of relief the statute already granted. Never sold as an expungement packet.

routes.mechanism: Nonconviction expungement for dismissal, no disposition, or acquittal

timing.anchorText: relief opens on the qualifying dismissal, dropped charge, closed no-disposition matter, or acquittal; the no-disposition branch needs reliable closure proof

requiredFacts: Was there an arrest and release?
What was the exact outcome and its date?
Any pending charge, appeal, or related count?
Is proof of the disposition available?
routes.notes: Use subsection (4). Reject the stale subsection (2)/(3) packet labels.

routes.mechanism: Nonadjudication under § 99-15-26 — admission while the case is active

timing.anchorText: admission is active-case and discretionary; no elapsed wait applies at this stage

requiredFacts: Is this the admission stage or a completed matter?
What is the offense and does an exclusion apply?
Any DUI, implied consent, or trafficking element?
exclusions: No trafficking, implied-consent, or DUI misuse
routes.notes: No checkout before completion and closure.

routes.mechanism: Nonadjudication under § 99-15-26 — expungement after completion and closure

timing.anchorText: relief opens on the later of court-certified completion and the dismissal or closure order

requiredFacts: What is the offense and does an exclusion apply?
Any DUI, implied consent, or trafficking element?
Is there a dismissal or closure order?
exclusions: No trafficking, implied-consent, or DUI misuse
routes.notes: Separated from active admission. Checkout opens only after completion and closure.

routes.mechanism: Pretrial intervention or diversion — admission while the case is active

timing.anchorText: admission is active-case; entry depends on district attorney and program acceptance, not on any elapsed wait

requiredFacts: Is the person represented by counsel?
Has the district attorney or program accepted the person?
What is the charge and does an exclusion apply?
exclusions: Age, indictment, counsel and program-acceptance conditions
routes.notes: Referral and guidance only. Checkout opens only after a qualifying disposition.

routes.mechanism: Pretrial intervention or diversion — expungement after completion and qualifying disposition

timing.anchorText: relief opens on the later of program completion and the dismissal, dropped-charge, or no-disposition event

requiredFacts: What is the charge and does an exclusion apply?
routes.notes: Admission, completion and expungement are separate stages.

routes.mechanism: Additional justice- or municipal-court misdemeanor relief — court selection between the two variants

timing.anchorText: two years of good conduct measured from the date of the person's last conviction in any court

requiredFacts: Was the target case in justice court or municipal court?
What is the full conviction history?
What is the date of the last conviction anywhere?
Has there been any later conviction?
routes.notes: Retained as the selection route only; the justice-court and municipal-court variants are separate contracts under different statutes. Use the last-conviction clock, not sentence completion.

routes.mechanism: Additional justice-court misdemeanor relief

timing.anchorText: two years of good conduct measured from the date of the person's last conviction in any court

requiredFacts: Which justice-court cases are being targeted?
What is the full conviction history?
What is the date of the last conviction anywhere?
Has there been any later conviction?
How will the prosecutor be noticed?
routes.notes: Use the last-conviction clock, not sentence completion.

routes.mechanism: Additional municipal-court misdemeanor relief

timing.anchorText: two years of good conduct measured from the date of the person's last conviction in any court

requiredFacts: Which municipal-court cases are being targeted?
What is the full conviction history?
What is the date of the last conviction anywhere?
Has there been any later conviction?
How will the prosecutor be noticed?
routes.notes: Use the last-conviction clock, not sentence completion.

routes.mechanism: First-offense DUI expungement

timing.anchorText: five years after successful completion of every ordered condition

requiredFacts: Does the person hold a CDL or CLP?
routes.notes: Keep the five-year rule only on this route; it never applies to DUI nonadjudication.

routes.mechanism: Minor-in-possession / underage-alcohol expungement

timing.anchorText: one year after the dismissal or discharge date on the dismissal branch, or one year after the later of full completion and payment of the fine on the conviction branch

requiredFacts: Is this the dismissal branch or the conviction branch?
routes.notes: Use the one-year route-specific rule only. The clock anchor depends on the disposition branch, which is why both anchors are named.

routes.mechanism: Uncharged or unprosecuted misdemeanor — no-charge branch

timing.anchorText: twelve months after the arrest or citation date where no formal charge or prosecution has followed

requiredFacts: What is the arrest or citation date?
Has there been any prosecution activity?
exclusions: No charge or prosecution during the twelve months
routes.notes: The twelve-month clock applies to the no-charge branch only. Register route key alias: MS:uncharged-or-unprosecuted-misdemeanor-after-12-months.

routes.mechanism: Uncharged or unprosecuted misdemeanor — dismissal branch

timing.anchorText: relief opens immediately upon dismissal; no elapsed wait applies to this branch

requiredFacts: Was the charge dismissed and on what date?
routes.notes: Dismissal is immediate. Never apply the twelve-month no-charge clock here.
